annotations.description: With a hand containing no 1-drop creatures and a curve starting at 2 mana (Deep-Cavern Bat), choosing to play first means drawing one fewer card. The hand has Kaito (4 mana) and two Deep-Cavern Bats but limited early pressure and no turn-1 play. On the draw, the extra card could help find additional lands or action. However, going first does allow Turn 2 Deep-Cavern Bat to strip a card before the opponent develops, which is a legitimate tempo play. This is close but the hand's mana base (Island, Swamp, Multiversal Passage, Soulstone Sanctuary) is a bit awkward and an extra draw could help smooth things out.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to play first (MiMo Gramps goes first)
annotations.betterLine: Going first is defensible with Turn 2 Deep-Cavern Bat for hand disruption, but going on the draw for the extra card with this somewhat clunky hand was worth considering.

annotations.description: Playing Multiversal Passage on turn 1 when there are no turn-1 plays wastes the flexibility of this dual-purpose land. With Island, Swamp, and Soulstone Sanctuary also in hand, playing a basic land first preserves Multiversal Passage's ability to fill whatever color gap emerges later. The hand wants B on turn 2 for Deep-Cavern Bat and UB by turn 4 for Kaito — playing Swamp turn 1 achieves the same curve while keeping Multiversal Passage flexible.
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp turn 1, preserving Multiversal Passage's flexibility to fill whatever color is needed later in the game.

By choosing Island for Multiversal Passage, they'll have two Islands and one Swamp, making it harder to curve out with Deep-Cavern Bat on turn 2 (needing to play Swamp turn 1 or 2 specifically). Choosing Swamp would give them two black sources and one blue source, which better supports casting Deep-Cavern Bat on turn 2 while still having Island available for Kaito later. The redundant Island is less valuable than a second Swamp given the hand composition.

annotations.betterLine: Choose Swamp to have two black sources for reliable turn 2 Deep-Cavern Bat, since Island is already in hand for blue mana

The opponent's board was just a Llanowar Elves with no untapped blue mana for counterplay.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority during combat without casting anything, missing the Enduring Curiosity flash opportunity.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Enduring Curiosity with flash before combat damage resolves to draw 2 cards from the two creatures dealing combat damage, generating significant card advantage.

annotations.description: MiMo Gramps spent 4 mana to animate Soulstone Sanctuary into a 3/3 vigilance creature instead of casting Enduring Curiosity (4/3 flash with massive card draw potential). With Floodpits Drowner and Deep-Cavern Bat already on board, Enduring Curiosity would draw cards whenever any creature deals combat damage, providing significant card advantage. The opponent is at 11 life with almost no board, making the card advantage engine extremely powerful. Enduring Curiosity is also resilient to removal (returns as enchantment when it dies).
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Soulstone Sanctuary for 4 mana to make it a 3/3 vigilance creature.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Enduring Curiosity for {2}{U}{U} using the available 2U+B+C mana. This provides a larger body (4/3), draws cards on every combat damage from any creature, and is resilient to removal. Alternatively, cast Deep-Cavern Bat for {1}{B} to strip an opponent's card while keeping 2 mana open.

annotations.description: Discarding Spider-Sense, the only counterspell/interaction piece in hand, against a UB control/tempo deck that likely has removal spells and threats like Kaito. With 5 mana creatures already in hand (2 Spider Manifestation, 2 Gene Pollinator, 1 Llanowar Elves) plus one on board, discarding a redundant mana dork would preserve the ability to interact with the opponent's key spells.
annotations.betterLine: Discard a redundant mana creature like the second Gene Pollinator or the extra Llanowar Elves, keeping Spider-Sense as the only interactive spell to counter key opponent removal or threats.

annotations.description: MiMo Gramps used Shoot the Sheriff to kill Llanowar Elves during combat instead of using Kaito's Ninjutsu ability to put Kaito onto the battlefield as an unblocked attacker. With Floodpits Drowner attacking unblocked, Ninjutsu for {1}{U}{B} would deploy a 3/4 hexproof threat that generates emblems and card advantage. The available mana (Island, Swamp, Multiversal Passage as Island, Soulstone Sanctuary) likely couldn't support both plays, making this a choice between killing a 1/1 mana dork and deploying a game-winning planeswalker.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Shoot the Sheriff targeting Llanowar Elves during combat
annotations.betterLine: Use Kaito's Ninjutsu ({1}{U}{B}) to return unblocked Floodpits Drowner to hand and put Kaito onto the battlefield tapped and attacking, dealing 3 damage and enabling loyalty abilities. Shoot the Sheriff could be saved for a later turn or a more important target.

annotations.description: MiMo Gramps used Shoot the Sheriff to destroy the opponent's Llanowar Elves instead of one of their own creatures that was a valid target. Shoot the Sheriff says 'Destroy target non-outlaw creature' — it can target any non-outlaw creature on either side. However, looking at the context more carefully: MiMo Gramps is the one casting Shoot the Sheriff, so they're choosing what to kill. Llanowar Elves is the opponent's mana dork, while Floodpits Drowner and Deep-Cavern Bat are MiMo's own creatures. Killing the opponent's Llanowar Elves removes their mana acceleration when they're already at 11 life with only 2 lands. However, this is being cast during MiMo's own combat phase, which means MiMo spent mana on removal during their own attack step rather than before or after combat. More importantly, the Deep-Cavern Bat is tapped (likely attacked or just entered), and Floodpits Drowner could have attacked. The real question is whether killing Llanowar Elves was the right target — and it actually seems reasonable since it denies the opponent mana. But casting a removal spell during your own combat phase is unusual timing. Actually, re-reading: the opponent has Spider-Sense in graveyard, so no counterspell threat. Killing Llanowar Elves to deny mana when the opponent is at 11 life and only has 2 lands is actually a reasonable play to keep them constrained. This seems fine.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Llanowar Elves with Shoot the Sheriff during own combat phase
annotations.betterLine: This is actually reasonable — denying the opponent's only mana acceleration when they're land-light keeps them constrained. The timing during combat is slightly awkward but the target choice is defensible.

annotations.description: Paid 2 life for Breeding Pool to enter untapped at 8 life when facing 3 damage per turn from opponent's creatures. The extra untapped mana enables casting an additional 1-drop alongside a 2-drop, but at 8 life (going to 6), every life point is critical. With 2 lands already available, they could still cast their key 2-mana plays (Badgermole Cub or Spider Manifestation) without the life payment.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Breeding Pool untapped, paying 2 life (8 → 6 life)
annotations.betterLine: Play Breeding Pool tapped (staying at 8 life), then cast a 2-drop like Badgermole Cub or Spider Manifestation with the existing 2 untapped lands. Preserving 2 life is more important than the marginal tempo of an extra 1-drop when at such low life.

annotations.description: With the opponent having no untapped creatures to block and no mana available for instant-speed interaction, attacking with only Breeding Pool instead of all available creatures leaves free damage on the table. Spider Manifestation could attack for 2 additional damage risk-free.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Breeding Pool, holding back Spider Manifestation
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all creatures (Breeding Pool and Spider Manifestation) since the opponent has no blockers and no mana up, dealing 2 additional damage for free. If mana from Spider Manifestation was needed post-combat, the 'whenever you cast a spell with mana value 4 or greater, untap this creature' ability wouldn't help here, and the tapped lands limit post-combat options anyway.

annotations.description: MiMo Gramps missed lethal. Opponent is at 5 life with only Spider Manifestation (2/2 reach) as a blocker and all lands tapped. By using Kaito's +1 (making him a 4/5 Ninja with the emblem), then casting Requiting Hex (B) to destroy Spider Manifestation (mana value 2), then attacking with Kaito (4/5) and Deep-Cavern Bat (1/1 flying) for exactly 5 damage = lethal. Instead, they played a tapped land and skipped their attack entirely.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Soulstone Sanctuary and skipped the attack phase entirely.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Kaito +1 for the Ninja emblem (Kaito becomes 4/5), cast Requiting Hex targeting Spider Manifestation to destroy it, then attack with Kaito (4/5) and Deep-Cavern Bat (1/1) for exactly 5 lethal damage.

annotations.description: MiMo Gramps missed lethal. Opponent is at 5 life with only Spider Manifestation (2/2 reach, MV 2) as a blocker. Requiting Hex destroys creatures with MV 2 or less, clearing the blocker. Then activating Soulstone Sanctuary (4 mana) to make it a 3/3 and attacking with Kaito (3/4) + Deep-Cavern Bat (1/1) + Soulstone creature (3/3) = 7 damage, lethal against 5 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Deep-Cavern Bat instead of going for the lethal line.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Requiting Hex targeting Spider Manifestation (MV 2), activate Soulstone Sanctuary for 4 mana to make it a 3/3, then attack with Kaito (3) + Deep-Cavern Bat (1) + Soulstone Sanctuary (3) for 7 total damage, dealing lethal to the opponent at 5 life.

annotations.description: Attacking with Deep-Cavern Bat (which is exiling Craterhoof Behemoth) alongside Kaito risks the opponent blocking and killing the bat to get Craterhoof back, all for just 1 extra damage when the opponent is at 5 life and this doesn't represent lethal. While the opponent at 5 life with minimal board may struggle to cast Craterhoof soon, unnecessarily risking the return of an 8-mana game-ending threat for marginal damage is suboptimal.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with all creatures including the Deep-Cavern Bat holding Craterhoof Behemoth in exile
annotations.betterLine: Attack with only Kaito, Bane of Nightmares. If Spider Manifestation blocks, it dies and clears the way for lethal next turn. If unblocked, opponent goes to 2 life. Either way, Craterhoof stays exiled safely.

annotations.description: Discarded Craterhoof Behemoth, which is their only win condition. At 1 life the game is desperate, but Craterhoof is the only card that can convert a board of small creatures into a lethal attack. With mana creatures in hand and on board, reaching 8 mana was achievable within 1-2 turns. Without Craterhoof, there is essentially no path to winning.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Craterhoof Behemoth to hand size
annotations.betterLine: Discard a redundant Spider Manifestation or Llanowar Elves instead. Craterhoof is the deck's only win condition and with multiple mana creatures available, casting it was a realistic possibility within 1-2 turns.
